newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-COLONIAL RACES TOWARD PROFIT FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-COLONIAL RACES TOWARD PROFIT FORECAST.

text.p: Australia's newly listed life insurance and banking group Colonial Ltd on Thursday reported a bumper half-year profit of A$118 million and said it could exceed its forecast for annual earnings of A$180 million.
In its first profit report as a listed company, Colonial said it was on target to meet or even exceed the profit forecast given to investors this year when it went to the stock market.
"In the existing market environment, the company is on target to meet, if not exceed, prospectus forecasts," managing director Peter Smedley said in a statement.

Helped by gravity-defying investment markets and a crackdown on costs, Colonial's net profit after tax of A$118 million for the six months ended June 30 was already 65 percent of the way towards the full-year forecast.
One share analyst on Thursday agreed Colonial was likely to exceed the forecast, but a steep fall in investment markets could still put it beyond reach.
"You would think it's more likely that it will exceed (the forecast) than not, but if you had a really bad second half for investment markets then it's not a given...," he told Reuters.
Colonial reported a rise in new premium business across Australia, New Zealand, Britain and Asia, as well as a drop in the cost of writing these new policies.

Colonial State Bank reported a 22 percent rise in net profit after tax to A$57.1 million, partly reflecting an improvement in its cost to income ratio to 66.4 percent at June 30 from 74.1 percent a year earlier.
The bank's operating expenses fell 15 percent, or A$37 million, against the same half last year.
Operating expenses also fell across the Australian, New Zealand and U.K. insurance and superannuation businesses, by over A$11 million in the half year, Colonial said.

Management expenses for Colonial Investment Management were also lower as a percentage of revenue. For the group, earnings per ordinary share were 20.2 cents per share for the half year, against a full year prospectus forecast of 28.4 cents per share.
Funds under management rose to A$43.4 billion at June 30, up 13 percent or A$4.9 billion from December 31
Colonial also reported a 37 percent increase in its embedded value to A$896 million at June 30, largely due to the move to 100 percent control of its Asian business.
Embedded value is a benchmark measure of the value of a life company, taking into account both the present value of existing premiums and the value of new business yet to be written.

The embedded value rose A$243 million from A$653 million at December 31, of which A$215 million of new value was added when Colonial bought out its Asian life insurance joint venture this year from Jardine Pacific for US$163 million.
The rest came from lower costs of writing new business and flatter commission structures, Colonial said.
Shares in Colonial, which listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in May, were nine cents higher at A$3.49 at 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT) on Thursday.
